To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adaptive differentiation of salt glands in birds involves a progressive tuning of the signal transduction pathway that leads to an increase in cytosol-free calcium concentrations ([ Ca2+]i), so that the pathway is uniquely tuned to the cells' requirements for a particular response.

the supraorbital salt glands of birds respond to salt loading by an adaptive increase in secretory performance, and this adaptive increase is achieved by a progressive increase in the secretory cell's capacity to generate an increase in cytosol-free calcium concentration ([Ca2+] i) in response to the muscarinic receptor-mediated activation of phospholipase C.

the supraorbital nasal salt glands in birds are able to produce a rapid and sustained response to an acute salt challenge, and a slower, progressive response to a chronic salt challenge, both of which require an increase in [ Ca2+]i.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the salt gland responds to salt loads and how these mechanisms differ in the short and long-term.
the mechanisms of salt secretion by salt glands and how they are controlled.
the elucidation of the mechanisms that regulate the secretory performance of vertebrate salt glands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cells have the capacity to generate the appropriate response to a given stimulus (i.e., the increase in [Ca 2+]i) by altering their sensitivity to the signal and/or the nature of the response.
the salt gland cells are capable of producing the appropriate response to a salt load, but only if the cells have been previously adapted to a salt load.

the adaptive differentiation of the secretory cells of salt glands is a process that involves a progressive modification of the signaling pathways that are responsible for the generation and processing of the signals that control the secretory performance of the gland, in response to the specific requirements of the cells in the new environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cells are able to respond in different ways to the same stimulus by altering the way the stimulus is transduced into the appropriate response.
the cells of the salt gland are able to respond to an osmoregulatory challenge in a variety of ways, depending on the severity and nature of the challenge and their current state of adaptation.
the cells have evolved to use the same signal (i.e. increase in [Ca(2+)](i)) to generate different types of response, and the cells' ability to do this is a key feature of the adaptive process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cells of the supra-orbitional gland have the ability to tune the signaling pathway that generates the [Ca2+] response, to the requirements of the cells.
a signaling system as simple as the increase in [Ca]i can be used to produce a wide range of different responses by cells.

the cells of salt glands have evolved a highly sophisticated mechanism for integrating signals from the nervous system with their own developmental state in order to generate a response that is appropriate to the cells' current requirements.
